results.label: No Symptoms Reported
results.summary: You have not reported any PMS symptoms. Your hormonal cycle appears to be well-balanced at this time.
results.body: Not experiencing PMS symptoms is a good sign that your progesterone and oestrogen levels are in healthy balance during your luteal phase. Hormonal balance can be affected by stress, diet, sleep, and age, so it is worth keeping an eye on symptoms if anything changes.

steps.title: Maintain your healthy habits
steps.body: Regular exercise, a low-sugar diet, quality sleep, and stress management are the foundations of hormonal health — keep them up.

steps.title: Know the signs
steps.body: PMS symptoms can develop or worsen with age, especially in your 30s and 40s as progesterone levels begin to fluctuate.

steps.title: Annual hormone check
steps.body: A simple hormone panel once a year gives you a clear baseline and helps catch any imbalances before they become problematic.

results.verdict: You have not reported any PMS symptoms. Your hormonal cycle appears to be well-balanced at this time.

results.label: Mild Symptoms
results.summary: You are experiencing mild PMS symptoms. These are likely manageable but may still affect your comfort and mood in the days before your period.
results.body: Mild PMS is most commonly caused by the natural drop in progesterone in the second half of your cycle. Symptoms such as fluid retention, breast tenderness, mild irritability, and fatigue are very common and often respond well to dietary adjustments, magnesium supplementation, and regular exercise. A hormone panel can confirm whether a progesterone imbalance is contributing to your symptoms.

steps.title: Try targeted supplementation
steps.body: Magnesium glycinate (300–400mg/day), vitamin B6, and evening primrose oil are evidence-based supplements shown to reduce mild PMS symptoms significantly.

steps.title: Reduce sugar and caffeine
steps.body: Blood sugar swings and caffeine both amplify PMS symptoms. Reducing intake in the week before your period can make a noticeable difference.

steps.title: Consider a hormone panel
steps.body: A female hormone panel measuring progesterone, oestradiol, and DHEA-S will confirm whether low progesterone in your luteal phase is driving your symptoms.

results.verdict: You are experiencing mild PMS symptoms. These are likely manageable but may still affect your comfort and mood in the days before your period.

results.label: Moderate to Severe Symptoms
results.summary: Your symptoms are significantly impacting your quality of life. This level of PMS often indicates a hormone imbalance that would benefit from professional assessment and treatment.
results.body: A score in this range suggests oestrogen dominance or progesterone deficiency — the most common hormonal drivers of moderate-to-severe PMS. You may be experiencing a combination of physical symptoms (bloating, breast pain, headaches, joint pain) alongside emotional symptoms (mood swings, anxiety, depression, irritability). These are not "normal" and do not need to be tolerated. Bioidentical progesterone therapy, alongside targeted nutritional support, has an excellent track record in significantly reducing symptoms at this level.

steps.title: Get a comprehensive hormone panel
steps.body: A full female hormone profile including progesterone, oestradiol, testosterone, DHEA-S, cortisol, and thyroid will identify exactly which imbalances are driving your symptoms.

steps.title: Speak to a specialist
steps.body: Our healthcare specialists understand the complexity of PMS and can discuss bioidentical progesterone therapy, dietary strategies, and evidence-based supplements tailored to your results.

steps.title: Track your cycle symptoms
steps.body: Keep a daily diary noting symptom severity across your cycle. This helps your clinician identify the pattern and confirm a PMS diagnosis versus other hormonal conditions.

results.verdict: Your symptoms are significantly impacting your quality of life. This level of PMS often indicates a hormone imbalance that would benefit from professional assessment and treatment.

results.label: Minimal Adrenal Load
results.summary: Your score suggests a low level of adrenal stress at this time. Your cortisol and adrenal function appear to be coping well with your current demands.
results.body: A low score indicates that your stress response system is not significantly overloaded right now. Your adrenal glands — which produce cortisol, DHEA, and adrenaline — appear to be functioning within a healthy range. Maintaining the habits that support this is key: regular sleep, balanced nutrition, moderate exercise, and effective stress management practices. It is still worth monitoring these symptoms over time, as adrenal stress can develop gradually.
results.verdict: Your score suggests a low level of adrenal stress at this time. Your cortisol and adrenal function appear to be coping well with your current demands.

results.label: Mild to Moderate Adrenal Stress
results.summary: You are experiencing some signs of adrenal stress. Your body is managing, but the early warning signs of adrenal dysfunction are present — particularly fatigue, irritability, anxiety, and disrupted sleep.
results.body: A score in this range suggests your HPA axis (hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis) is under moderate strain. Sustained stress causes cortisol to remain elevated for extended periods, which disrupts sleep, depletes energy, increases anxiety, and eventually leads to adrenal fatigue as cortisol output begins to decline. At this stage, targeted nutritional support, lifestyle changes, and an adrenal hormone panel can make a significant difference before the condition progresses. DHEA levels in particular tend to drop as cortisol demands increase, and restoring DHEA can meaningfully improve energy, mood, and resilience.
results.verdict: You are experiencing some signs of adrenal stress. Your body is managing, but the early warning signs of adrenal dysfunction are present — particularly fatigue, irritability, anxiety, and disrupted sleep.

results.label: Moderate to Severe Adrenal Fatigue
results.summary: Your score indicates significant adrenal dysfunction. The symptoms you are experiencing — persistent exhaustion, emotional dysregulation, anxiety, poor sleep, and afternoon energy crashes — are hallmarks of adrenal fatigue that require attention.
results.body: At this level, your adrenal glands have been under prolonged stress and are likely producing abnormal cortisol patterns — either chronically elevated (early-stage) or depleted (late-stage adrenal fatigue). Both patterns produce overlapping symptoms but respond to different interventions, which is why a proper adrenal hormone panel is essential. The cascade of effects from dysregulated cortisol is wide-ranging: it disrupts thyroid function, sex hormone production (lowering testosterone and progesterone), immune function, blood sugar regulation, and sleep architecture. A comprehensive hormonal assessment alongside targeted adrenal support is strongly recommended.
results.verdict: Your score indicates significant adrenal dysfunction. The symptoms you are experiencing — persistent exhaustion, emotional dysregulation, anxiety, poor sleep, and afternoon energy crashes — are hallmarks of adrenal fatigue that require attention.

results.label: Severe Adrenal Exhaustion
results.summary: Your score is at the maximum level, indicating severe adrenal exhaustion. Every symptom assessed is occurring constantly. This requires immediate clinical attention.
results.body: Scoring at the maximum level suggests your adrenal glands are severely depleted. Adrenal exhaustion — sometimes called stage 3 adrenal fatigue — is characterised by extremely low cortisol output, profound fatigue that does not improve with rest, intense anxiety or emotional numbness, complete inability to sleep restoratively, and crashing energy levels. Without intervention, this state can significantly impair your immune function, cardiovascular health, metabolic health, and quality of life. Recovery is possible but takes time, the right treatment, and professional guidance. Please reach out to one of our specialists as soon as possible.
results.verdict: Your score is at the maximum level, indicating severe adrenal exhaustion. Every symptom assessed is occurring constantly. This requires immediate clinical attention.

results.label: Lower Risk Profile
results.summary: You have few identified risk factors for osteoporosis. Maintaining your current protective habits and monitoring bone health periodically is recommended.
results.body: Your responses suggest a lower risk profile for osteoporosis at this time. With fewer than four risk factors identified, your bone density is less likely to be significantly compromised — particularly if you are maintaining a regular exercise routine and meeting your daily calcium requirements. That said, bone loss is a gradual process that begins earlier than most people realise. Establishing your bone density baseline with a DEXA scan, especially if you are over 40, is a proactive step that gives you a clear picture of your current bone health and a reference point for the future.

steps.title: Maintain weight-bearing exercise
steps.body: Activities like walking, jogging, resistance training, and dancing stimulate bone formation. Aim for at least 30 minutes most days.

steps.title: Optimise your calcium and vitamin D intake
steps.body: Calcium (1000–1200mg/day) and vitamin D3 (1000–2000 IU/day) are the foundation of bone health. Consider a bone health panel to check your current levels.

steps.title: Consider a baseline DEXA scan
steps.body: A DEXA scan measures your bone mineral density and is the gold standard for detecting low bone density before fractures occur. Recommended from age 40 onwards.

results.verdict: You have few identified risk factors for osteoporosis. Maintaining your current protective habits and monitoring bone health periodically is recommended.

results.label: Elevated Risk Profile
results.summary: You have identified multiple risk factors for osteoporosis. We recommend a bone density assessment and a consultation with a specialist to discuss prevention and treatment options.
results.body: Your responses indicate an elevated risk profile for osteoporosis, with four or more risk factors identified. Osteoporosis is often called the "silent disease" because bone loss occurs gradually and without symptoms — until a fracture happens. The good news is that with the right assessment, lifestyle changes, and treatment where needed, bone loss can be significantly slowed or even reversed. Key factors in your profile — which may include postmenopausal status, low testosterone, physical inactivity, smoking, high alcohol or caffeine intake, or a family history of osteoporosis — are all clinically recognised contributors to reduced bone mineral density. Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) has strong evidence for protecting bone density, particularly in women around menopause, as does testosterone replacement in men with low levels. A comprehensive bone health assessment including a DEXA scan and hormone panel is the recommended first step.

steps.title: Get a DEXA bone density scan
steps.body: A DEXA scan is the most accurate way to measure bone mineral density and determine your actual fracture risk. It is quick, painless, and widely available.

steps.title: Get a hormone and bone health panel
steps.body: Low oestrogen, low testosterone, low vitamin D, and low calcium absorption are the key hormonal and nutritional drivers of bone loss. A comprehensive panel identifies exactly which factors apply to you.

steps.title: Speak to a specialist about treatment
steps.body: Depending on your results, options may include hormone replacement therapy (HRT), bisphosphonates, calcium and vitamin D supplementation, and structured exercise programmes — all with strong evidence for protecting and rebuilding bone density.

results.verdict: You have identified multiple risk factors for osteoporosis. We recommend a bone density assessment and a consultation with a specialist to discuss prevention and treatment options.

results.label: No Symptoms Reported
results.summary: You have not reported any menopause symptoms at this time. This is a positive result — though it is worth monitoring for changes as you move through your 40s and 50s.
results.body: Your responses suggest you are not currently experiencing symptoms associated with menopause. Hormonal changes during and after menopause can develop gradually, and establishing a hormone baseline now — even without symptoms — provides a valuable reference point for the future. We recommend a female hormone panel as part of your routine health assessment, alongside maintaining bone density, cardiovascular health, and hormonal wellness through regular exercise, a nutrient-rich diet, and good sleep hygiene.

steps.title: Establish a hormone baseline
steps.body: A female hormone panel measuring FSH, LH, oestradiol, and progesterone gives you a clear starting point — even before symptoms develop.

steps.title: Protect your long-term health
steps.body: Declining oestrogen after menopause increases the risk of osteoporosis and cardiovascular disease. Early lifestyle investment pays dividends later.

steps.title: Know the signs
steps.body: Familiarise yourself with menopause symptoms so you can act early if they arise. Hot flashes, sleep disruption, and mood changes are often the first indicators.

results.verdict: You have not reported any menopause symptoms at this time. This is a positive result — though it is worth monitoring for changes as you move through your 40s and 50s.

results.label: Mild to Moderate Symptoms
results.summary: You are experiencing a number of symptoms that may be linked to menopause. A hormone evaluation would help clarify whether declining oestrogen and progesterone levels are contributing to how you feel.
results.body: Menopause causes a wide range of symptoms as oestrogen, progesterone, and testosterone levels decline — from physical changes such as hot flashes, vaginal dryness, and weight gain to emotional and cognitive changes including mood swings, anxiety, and reduced concentration. Many women normalise these symptoms or attribute them to ageing, stress, or other causes. A comprehensive hormone panel will give you and your healthcare provider a clear picture of your current hormonal status, and there are several highly effective, evidence-based treatment options available — including bioidentical hormone replacement therapy (BHRT) — that can significantly reduce or eliminate the symptoms you are experiencing.

steps.title: Get a comprehensive hormone panel
steps.body: A full female hormone profile measuring FSH, LH, oestradiol, progesterone, testosterone, DHEA-S, and thyroid will identify exactly which hormones are declining and driving your symptoms.

steps.title: Speak to a specialist
steps.body: Our healthcare specialists can review your results privately and discuss options including bioidentical HRT, which closely mirrors your body's natural hormones for effective, well-tolerated symptom relief.

steps.title: Track your symptoms
steps.body: Keep a diary noting which symptoms occur, their severity, and when they happen. This helps your clinician identify patterns and confirm menopause versus other hormonal conditions.

results.verdict: You are experiencing a number of symptoms that may be linked to menopause. A hormone evaluation would help clarify whether declining oestrogen and progesterone levels are contributing to how you feel.

results.label: Significant Symptoms
results.summary: You are reporting a high number of menopause symptoms that are significantly impacting your quality of life. We strongly recommend a hormone assessment and specialist consultation as soon as possible.
results.body: Scoring 15 or more symptoms indicates that menopause is having a substantial impact across multiple areas of your health and daily functioning. The wide range of symptoms you are experiencing — which may include hot flashes, severe sleep disruption, mood and cognitive changes, vaginal dryness, reduced libido, pain, and cardiovascular or bone health risk factors — are all well-documented consequences of declining oestrogen and progesterone. You do not have to manage these symptoms alone, and you do not have to simply endure them. Bioidentical hormone replacement therapy (BHRT) has decades of evidence demonstrating its effectiveness for reducing menopause symptoms and protecting long-term bone and cardiovascular health. The first step is a comprehensive hormone panel so we understand exactly where your levels stand — and then our specialists can build a personalised treatment plan around your specific results and health profile.

steps.title: Comprehensive hormone panel — as soon as possible
steps.body: A full female hormone profile including FSH, LH, oestradiol, progesterone, testosterone, DHEA-S, cortisol, and thyroid gives the clearest picture of your hormonal status and treatment needs.

steps.title: Book a free specialist consultation
steps.body: Our specialists are experienced in managing complex menopause presentations and can discuss BHRT, lifestyle interventions, targeted supplementation, and bone and cardiovascular protection strategies.

steps.title: Address bone and heart health now
steps.body: With risk factors for both osteoporosis and heart disease identified, early intervention is critical. Declining oestrogen directly and rapidly affects both — and BHRT has strong evidence for protecting both simultaneously.

results.verdict: You are reporting a high number of menopause symptoms that are significantly impacting your quality of life. We strongly recommend a hormone assessment and specialist consultation as soon as possible.
